newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end lower as early buying fizzles out.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end lower as early buying fizzles out.

text.p: Kuala Lumpur shares closed lower as early buying fizzled out on fears of profit-taking on Wall Street after Wednesday's rally, dealers said.
"People are worried that the Dow may come down as fast tonight as it appears to be toppish," said a bank-backed brokerage dealer. He said given the uncertainty, investors were quick to take profits.
A 96-point surge on Wall Street overnight had underpinned early sentiment, attracting some program buying by funds.
The key Composite Index closed at 1,177.93, down 1.16 points, after hitting a high of 1,186.56 in the morning.
Dealers said the index has been struggling to get past 1,190 and this was also a reason for the pull-back.
Second board stocks, which remained as the market focus, also gave back early gains. The Second Board index ended down 1.66 points at 637.39 after hitting an intraday all-time high of 645.52.
A drop in the shares of Tenaga Nasional, a major component stock, contributed to the fall in the Composite Index. The stock fell 50 cents to 10.50 ringgit.
